post.description:
Submits one or more external Naemon commands (schedule/cancel downtimes, acknowledge problems, force a recheck, ...) in a single request. The request body is a plain JSON array; each item is executed independently by the backend and items do not all need to use the same `command` value (mixed commands in one array are supported, live-verified 2026-08-10 against openITCOCKPIT 5.6.1). See the named request examples below for the exact fields each `command` expects.

Only the following `command` values are understood here: `submitHostDowntime`, `submitServiceDowntime`, `submitHoststateAck`, `submitServicestateAck`, `rescheduleHost`, `rescheduleService`, `commitPassiveResult`, `commitPassiveServiceResult`, `sendCustomHostNotification`, `sendCustomServiceNotification`, `enableOrDisableHostFlapdetection`, `enableOrDisableServiceFlapdetection`, `submitEnableHostNotifications`, `submitDisableHostNotifications`, `submitEnableServiceNotifications`, `submitDisableServiceNotifications`. The raw Naemon command names returned by `GET /nagios_module/cmd/index.json` (e.g. `SCHEDULE_HOST_DOWNTIME`, `ACKNOWLEDGE_HOST_PROBLEM`, `DEL_HOST_DOWNTIME`) are a different, unrelated vocabulary used by other, undocumented `nagios_module/cmd` actions and are rejected here with 400 "Could not send command".

A 200 response only confirms that the command(s) were handed off to the Naemon core, not that Naemon actually applied them: e.g. an `end` before `start` is queued the same way and is silently rejected and logged by Naemon (`Error: External command failed -> ...`) without surfacing as an API error. Always confirm the actual result via the matching GET endpoint (`GET /hosts/index.json`, `GET /services/index.json`, `GET /downtimes/host.json`, `GET /downtimes/service.json`, ...).

This endpoint has no command to delete a downtime or remove an acknowledgement. Existing downtimes are listed via `GET /downtimes/host.json` / `GET /downtimes/service.json` (field `internalDowntimeId`) and deleted via `POST /downtimes/delete/{id}.json`. Existing acknowledgements are listed via `GET /acknowledgements/host/{hostId}.json` / `GET /acknowledgements/service/{serviceId}.json` and removed via `POST /acknowledgements/delete/.json`.

bulkDowntimeMultipleObjects.description: Array items are executed independently; here two different services are put into downtime in one call. Items may also mix different `command` values.
bulkDowntimeMultipleObjects.summary: Schedule downtimes for several objects in a single request

bulkRescheduleServices.summary: Force an immediate recheck of several services in one request

hostAcknowledge.description: `hostAckType` selects `hostOnly` or `hostAndServices` (also acknowledges every currently non-OK service on that host). `sticky` is 0 (non-sticky) or 2 (sticky, per source code comment). The acknowledgement's `persistent` flag is always 1 server-side and cannot be changed through this endpoint. Naemon silently ignores this command if the host is not currently in a problem state.

hostDowntimeFixed.description: `downtimetype` 0 = host only (default), 1 = host incl. all of its services, 2/3 = propagate to dependent hosts (triggered / non-triggered). `start`/`end` are Unix timestamps in seconds. Downtimes created here are always fixed (Naemon's "flexible" downtime type is not exposed by this endpoint).

rescheduleHostForcedCheck.description: Reschedules the check for "now" (the server processes this asynchronously, so the actual check runs a few seconds after the request). There is no timestamp field. `type: hostAndServices` additionally force-reschedules every active service check on that host in the same call.
rescheduleHostForcedCheck.summary: Force an immediate recheck of a host

rescheduleServiceForcedCheck.summary: Force an immediate recheck of a single service

serviceAcknowledge.description: Live-verified against a service that was genuinely in a WARNING state.

serviceDowntime.description: Service downtimes have no `downtimetype` - they are always a plain fixed downtime for exactly this service.

200.description: The command(s) were queued. This does not guarantee Naemon accepted every item - see the endpoint description.

commandRejected.description: Live-verified with an unsupported `command` value and, separately, with a syntactically valid but non-existent hostUuid. Both produce this identical body.
commandRejected.summary: Unknown command value, or a hostUuid/serviceUuid Naemon could not resolve

#
# This is the configuration file for the openITCOCKPIT Monitoring Agent 3.x
# Notice: Empty values will not been ignored! If you want to disable an option like proxy comment it out!

#########################
#       Web Server      #
#########################

# Bind address of the build-in web server
# Use 0.0.0.0 to bind on all interfaces
address = 0.0.0.0

# Port of the Agents build-in web server
# Default port is 3333
port = 3333

#########################
#   Security Settings   #
#########################

# Try to enable auto ssl mode for webserver
try-autossl = False

# File paths used to store autossl related files (default: /etc/openitcockpit-agent/):
# Leave this blank to use the default values
# Example: /etc/openitcockpit-agent/agent.csr
#autossl-csr-file =

# Example: /etc/openitcockpit-agent/agent.crt
#autossl-crt-file =

# Example: /etc/openitcockpit-agent/agent.key
#autossl-key-file =

# Example: /etc/openitcockpit-agent/server_ca.crt
#autossl-ca-file =

# If a certificate file is given, the agent will only be accessible through HTTPS
# Instead of messing around with self-signed certificates we recommend to use the autossl feature.
# Example: /etc/ssl/certs/ssl-cert-snakeoil.pem
#certfile = /etc/ssl/certs/ssl-cert-snakeoil.pem

# Private key file of the given TLS certificate
# Example: /etc/ssl/private/ssl-cert-snakeoil.key
#keyfile = /etc/ssl/private/ssl-cert-snakeoil.key

# Enable remote read and write access to the current agent configuration (this file) and
# the customchecks config
# !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
# ! WARNING: This could lead to remote code execution    !
# !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
config-update-mode = False

# Enable HTTP Basic Authentication
# Example: auth = user:password
#auth = user:password

#########################
#        Checks         #
#########################

# Determines in seconds how often the agent will schedule all internal checks
interval = 30

# Remote Plugin Execution
# Path to config will where custom checks can be defined
# Comment to use the default value
#
# Linux: /etc/openitcockpit-agent/customchecks.ini
# Windows: C:\Program Files\it-novum\openitcockpit-agent\customchecks.ini
# macOS: /Applications/openitcockpit-agent/customchecks.ini
#customchecks = /etc/openitcockpit-agent/customchecks.ini

#########################
# Enable/Disable checks #
#########################

# Enable CPU monitoring
cpustats = True

# Enable memory monitoring
memory = True

# Enable Swap monitoring
swap = True

# Enable monitoring of running processes
processstats = True

# Enable monitoring of network interfaces
netstats = True

# Enable monitoring of the traffic (I/O) of network interfaces
netio = True

# Enable disk usage monitoring
diskstats = True

# Enable monitoring of disk I/O
diskio = True

# Enable monitoring of Systemd Services (Linux only)
systemdservices = True

# Enable monitoring of Launchd Services (macOS only)
launchdservices = True

# Enable monitoring of Windows Services (Windows only)
winservices = True

# Enable monitoring of Windows Event Log records (Windows only)
wineventlog = True

# Define comma separated windows event log log types
# Event Logs containing spaces DO NOT need to be quoted: Security,Sophos Cloud AD Sync,Application
wineventlog-logtypes = System,Application,Security

# Enable monitoring of temperature and battery sensors
sensorstats = True

# Enable support to monitor Docker containers
# Known issues: Error response from daemon: client version 1.41 is too new. Maximum supported API version is 1.40
# Workaround: export DOCKER_API_VERSION=1.40
dockerstats = False

# Check KVMs through libvirt
# This requires to complie the openITCOCKPIT Monitoring Agent by yourself.
# Please see the Wiki for instructions: https://github.com/it-novum/openitcockpit-agent-go/wiki/Build-binary
libvirt = True

# Enable logged in users check
userstats = True

#########################
#       Push mode       #
#########################

# By default openITCOCKPIT will pull check results from the openITCOCKPIT Agent.
# In a cloud environments or behind a NAT network it could become handy
# if the openITCOCKPIT Monitoring Agent will push the results to your openITCOCKPIT Server
[oitc]

# Enable Push Mode
enabled = True

# This option disables the webserver of the openITCOCKPIT Monitoring Agent when running in PUSH mode.
# When you also want to enable the Webserver even if the agent is running in PUSH mode we highly recommend
# to enable HTTP Basic Authentication and to use the certfile and keyfile options to enable HTTPS
enable-webserver = False

# Address of your openITCOCKPIT Server where the Agent will push the results to
# Example: https://demo.openitcockpit.io
url = https://127.0.0.1

# Enable this option when your openITCOCKPIT server uses valid TLS certificates
# like from Let's Encrypt
verify-server-certificate = False

# Timeout in seconds for the HTTP push client
timeout = 10

# API-Key of your openITCOCKPIT Server
apikey = <API_KEY>

# Address of HTTP/HTTPS Proxy if required.
# Comment to disable
# Example: http://10.10.1.10:3128
#proxy = http://10.10.1.10:3128
